sources_considered.why: Direct user study comparing model-assigned intent categories with participants' intentions.
Verified that the cited first version was publicly available on February 3, 2024.
The retrieved CLAMBER version uses GPT-4 in dataset construction; its general findings were not treated as a direct GPT-4 assistant evaluation.
The search result concerns GPT-4o end-to-end task performance, which neither isolates intent recognition nor matches the selected model scope.

evidence_items.locator: Section 5.1, Quality of Intent Recognition by State-of-the-Art LLMs
evidence_items.explanation: The January-dated manuscript reports 89.64% intent-category accuracy for GPT-4 Turbo against users' self-reported intentions. This is material evidence of successful mapping, but a taxonomy score does not establish whether a practical assistant meets its requirements.

unresolved_gaps: No practical acceptance threshold is supplied by the claim or established by the cited study.
The study measures intent categories rather than complete intended assistant actions.
The record does not establish reliability across representative production tasks with ordinary clarification.
The manuscript dates the report to January 2024 but does not specify the exact data-collection dates.
